# Product Defects

## Diagnostic steps before replacement

A widget that doesn't power on should go through the standard diagnostic
first: confirm the charging cable is seated fully, try a different power
outlet, and hold the reset button for 10 seconds. Only after the customer
confirms they've tried these steps (or explicitly declines to) should a
defect replacement be authorized - this keeps functioning units from being
scrapped over a loose cable.

## Defect replacement window

Unlike the refund window, the defect replacement window is 12 months from
the original purchase date, matching the hardware warranty. A defect
reported after 12 months is out of warranty and routed to L2 engineering
for a case-by-case call, not auto-resolved.

## Recurring defects on the same unit

If a customer reports a second defect on a replacement unit within 30 days
of receiving it, do not send a third like-for-like replacement
automatically - escalate to L2 engineering, since a repeat failure on a
freshly replaced unit can indicate a batch defect worth flagging to
manufacturing rather than another individual swap.

## Cosmetic issues are not defects

Minor cosmetic marks that don't affect function (a small scuff, uneven
paint on a non-functional trim piece) are not covered under the defect
policy and are not eligible for replacement.
